title: Lunar surface-to-LLO delta-v, propulsion and abort architecture audit for OTA-TEC-0084
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0084 document. Using primary, peer-reviewed and official lunar mission/engineering sources, assess: (1) representative delta-v requirements for powered descent from low lunar orbit to the surface and ascent back to LLO, clearly distinguishing orbital velocity, lunar escape velocity and mission delta-v; (2) gravity-loss, hover/divert, rendezvous and reserve contributions; (3) reusable lunar lander propellant and engine trade-offs relevant to a 2050s shuttle without validating a specific fictional vehicle; (4) throttling, landing-control and sensor requirements in vacuum; (5) realistic abort-to-orbit/abort-during-descent concepts and redundancy limits; and (6) whether a roughly 20-minute descent is operationally plausible as a fictional schedule. Identify wording that should be narrowed or reclassified. Do NOT evaluate or alter [F] introduction year, fleet size, accident statistics, traffic frequency, ticket prices, operators, Mars Credits, unlocks, journeys or other NOXIA balancing values.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0084 is now canonical and explicitly corrects the earlier misuse of lunar escape velocity as a surface-to-LLO delta-v proxy; the actual engineering envelope should now be source-pinned before game mappings harden.
real_world_anchor: Apollo LM powered descent/ascent, low lunar orbit mechanics, modern reusable lunar lander concepts, throttled rocket engines and abort-to-orbit architecture.
novelty_reason: First source-pinned propulsion and mission-delta-v audit of the canonical PELICAN lunar shuttle.
